$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. The known USB radio dongles of OneMind OS (issue #732). One table, read three ways: Go renders the image's udev rules from it (internal/detect/radios.go, os/rootfs/layers/onemind/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/70-onemind-radio.rules) and checks each named radio against it, and the gateway labels the radio-found cards (core/onemind_core/radios.py, GET /v1/radios). A dongle is matched by its USB vendor and product id AND its USB product string (a lowercase glob over the lowercased string), because cheap USB-serial chips share one id across many products. match=chip marks a row whose product string is the chip maker's default: any board with that chip looks the same, so the card says so. A USB serial line that matches no row is listed but never named and never granted. A new row is a contract change: add it here with its source, then run go test ./internal/detect -run TestRadioUdevRules -update.
name: /dev/onemind/{kind}-{usb_port}

kinds.zigbee-thread: an IEEE 802.15.4 radio that runs Zigbee or Thread firmware, one at a time; the USB ids do not say which
kinds.lora: a LoRa radio (Meshtastic or MeshCore firmware)

devices.model: SONOFF Zigbee 3.0 USB Dongle Plus V2
